generalized_learning.generalized_failure_pattern: A retention-backed report can appear covered by a generic temporal control while one aggregate tier uses a raw timestamp and its storage/query paths operate on a normalized bucket boundary.
generalized_learning.plausible_wrong_implementation: Treat all retention-backed reporting as one surface and reuse a control from one granularity for another, allowing daily, monthly or hourly boundary semantics to diverge silently.
generalized_learning.reusable_control: dedicated off-boundary reporting-availability control for every retained tier actually used by a report
generalized_learning.prevention_rule: Inventory every retained tier used by a coverage-reporting entrypoint, classify unused tiers explicitly, and derive purge, query and reported availability from one normalized boundary per tier.
generalized_learning.detection_rule: Reject shared controls across retained tiers and reject a bucketed-tier probe unless its cutoff is deliberately off-boundary and purge, query, reported availableFrom and boundary-state all resolve to the same normalized bucket.

transfer_cases.scenario: A day-bucket report receives a midday retention cutoff and must expose the retained day start consistently across purge, query and coverage.
A month-bucket report receives a mid-month retention cutoff and must expose the retained month start consistently across purge, query and coverage.

skill_changes.change: Retention-tier inference now accepts aggregate noun/adjective variants and coverage contracts require every retained reporting tier to be classified with a dedicated control when used.
Coverage validation rejects cross-tier control reuse, aligned-only probes, and any mismatch among normalized purge, query and reported availability boundaries.
